results.title: George Conway worried ailing Trump 'not even close to reality' anymore
results.description: Conservative attorney and President Donald Trump gadfly George Conway says there is no reason left to suspect the president has any real connection to reality anymore. This is not just a matter of Trump sleeping through briefings and public meetings. It’s a matter of psychosis. “There's a famous psychologist named Eric Fromm, who talked about malignant narcissists like Trump. I mean, the great evil people of history were malignant narcissists. And he basically says they tip into psychosis,” Conway told Bulwark podcaster Tim Miller . “They're basically psychotic because they want to believe the fantasy world in which they control everything and everything is about them. And that's where Trump has always been headed.” “And I think at this point, he's not even close to reality,” Cohen said. “And that's just a scary thing. And that's the thing that a little bothers me about the Natalie Harp episode is that people are treating this as a debate about whether it's a low blow by the Democrats.” Trump’s ubiquitous senior aid, dubbed the “human typewriter” or Trump’s “diaper nurse,” has been making news, most recently regarding her “extraordinary” and “unhinged” relationship with the octogenarian president. But Conway said this is more than some poor young woman and her intimate relationship with a confirmed adulterer . “It would be better if they were just having sex because it would ... be in the realm of normal human comprehension. But this is psychotic on both sides,” Conway told Miller. “She worships him as some kind of deity and he sucks that up and is using her as a tool to create and maintain his own fragile reality that is being tested each and every day.” Trump increasing use of bizarre claims and meandering moments are doing nothing to convince voters that a stable genius is occupying the White House. The president was recently speaking at a General Motors plant in Milford, Michigan, when he wandered into an anecdote about his father, Fred Trump, who died in 1999, that left onlookers scratching their heads. “I had a wonderful father, right, and he was a hard worker who was in the real estate business ... He didn’t want planes,” said Trump . “They didn’t have planes in those days, I don’t think.” The gaffes just keep coming, and Conway said his greatest fear is that the U.S. public is getting accustomed to having a maniac with a broken mind in the White House. “There's this kind of learned helplessness is what psychologists would call it,” said Conway. “We have reached this kind of what psychologists would call a malignant normality, where we're accepting things, we're accepting like a Watergate scandal, every level scandal, every week he does something that's just incredibly — that would be paralyzing of an administration for a month, or two, or a month, or end an administration, but he, you know, it's just, it's Tuesday.”

results.title: Luis Robert Jr. returns to a smattering of boos, and a White Sox team that's thrived without him
results.description:
Since he was signed as a lauded prospect in 2017, to winning a Gold Glove as a rookie for a seemingly ascendant playoff team in 2020, to the unfortunate role of being the most talented player on three-straight 100-plus loss teams, Luis Robert Jr. was always central to the White Sox.

“One of the guys I was really excited to manage, getting this job,” said White Sox manager Will Venable.

On Friday, he returned through the visitors entrance to Rate Field, to Sox teammates who view him warmly, to a brief tribute on the scoreboard, and as an afterthought.

After acquiring Robert as a win-now move this January, the Mets are having a disastrous season that cost manager Carlos Mendoza his job. That Robert remains after they sold at the trade deadline reflects his diminished trade value, due to the same issues that dogged his final years on the South Side.

“It’s very sad,” said his close friend, Miguel Vargas. “I feel like we could have seen one of the greatest baseball players on the field if he stayed healthy.”

For the third-straight year, Robert has been more hurt than good. A herniated disk in his back has limited him to 49 games this year and he’s struggled when available. He entered this weekend hitting just .215/.290/.362 with seven homers. With the Mets looking toward the future with young outfielders Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing, the still 29-year-old Robert, who used to range over to steal fly balls from Eloy Jiménez, was relegated to manning left field Friday.

“This season has been pretty similar to how other parts of my career have gone where I've been hurt, where I've been off the field,” Robert said via interpreter. “You prepare yourself all offseason to be healthy, you work on your body. For it to happen the way that it did this season, this is really disappointing."

A tattoo on Robert’s right knee commemorates his 2023 Silver Slugger-winning season, where his career-high 38 home runs was thought to cement himself as one of the game’s premier power threats and the centerpiece of the Sox lineup. Instead, Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery has hit more homers than Robert since that season (47 to 35), despite not debuting in the majors until July of 2025.

Montgomery is only third in homers on a White Sox offense that leads the American League in runs per game in Robert’s absence. The Sox have actually not received huge returns from the players the Mets sent back for Robert. Ironically, it’s hard-throwing Jordan Hicks, whose contract the Red Sox were also looking to shed this winter, who has been the most useful player the Sox were able to add after moving Robert’s $20 million salary.

More so it’s that Tristan Peters has provided stalwart center field defense and even made the AL All-Star team after being designated for assignment by the Rays and acquired for cash over the winter, that’s really demonstrated the wisdom in the Sox finally ceasing their efforts to revive Robert’s star potential.

But Sox players and coaches still look at Robert and see someone who was on the ground floor for the beginning of their turnaround last year, and could have fit in with their fun-loving ascent to playoff contention this summer.

Assuming he could’ve stayed healthy, that is. He couldn’t, obviously. He hoped there are no hard feelings about it. The smattering of boos mixed into his reception Friday night suggested otherwise.

“This is a team that I was with a long time and it will always have a special place in my heart, so I keep tabs on the results on the games and I'm really proud to see how they've been performing this season,” Robert said via interpreter. “Those last few years, we didn't get the job done the way that we wanted to. But at the same time, I can look back at it as a beautiful journey."

results.title: Volusia carjacking suspect held without bond after 137 mph chase
results.description: A 41-year-old man accused of pulling a woman from her car and leading law enforcement on a high-speed chase through Volusia County will remain behind bars after a judge ordered him held without bond Friday. Investigators say Scott Taylor was fleeing the Florida Highway Patrol when he stole a woman's car near Destination Daytona. Body camera video showed Taylor running toward the vehicle, forcing the woman out and driving away, according to authorities. Chase reaches 137 mph Authorities said Taylor then led officers on a pursuit that reached speeds of up to 137 mph. A truck driver caught up in the chase said the stolen car came off the interstate, crossed a median onto the wrong side of the road and clipped a dump truck before losing control. The car then slammed into the front of his truck. "The car basically came off the interstate, came across the median to the wrong side of the road, clipped the dump truck in front of me and lost control of the vehicle on the shoulder, came in sideways and hit the front of my truck," the driver said. Driver describes attempted carjacking The truck driver said Taylor got out after the crash and tried to enter his vehicle. The truck was locked, preventing Taylor from getting inside. "When he could not enter my vehicle, he ran straight back," the driver said. Body camera video showed officers chasing Taylor on foot and repeatedly ordering him to get on the ground before taking him into custody. Wife apologizes to victims Taylor appeared before a judge Friday and was ordered held without bond. His wife told FOX 35 after the hearing that the behavior was out of character and described Taylor as a "stand-up husband and father." She also apologized to those caught up in the incident. "I am so sorry that that happened to you. I thank the Lord that no one was hurt," she said. "It's so unfortunate and it's so sad." Taylor remained in the Volusia County jail Friday.
